note: Axis 3 executable-depth measurement for Mento Labs USDm on Celo. Celo and Monad are separate, non-fungible exit markets while NTT is not operational; no cross-chain liquidity is pooled.

identity.identity_note: This is the former cUSD contract renamed in place to USDm, not Mountain Protocol USDM or Monetrix USDM.

depth.basis: No depth figure is published. The venue is a fixed-price market maker: it returns an identical rate at every size, so there is no slippage curve to locate a 2% crossing on. The exit constraint is inventory and is reported in `exit_capacity` (currently $35,317.28), not as a depth figure with a different basis.

primary_exit.gated_basis: public router route; circuit breaker enabled and current trading limits have capacity
primary_exit.note: This venue is constrained by stateful trading limits. It should not be interpreted as conventional reserve-bounded secondary-market depth.

enumeration.source: Mento SDK canonical Celo route cache plus live Router and trading-limit reads
enumeration.chain_scope_note: Monad USDm liquidity is excluded because NTT is not operational and the markets cannot be combined into an executable exit.

venues.name: Mento V3 USDm/USDC
venues.depth_role: Canonical Celo exit route measured above; pool balance/TVL is not substituted for depth.

separate_market_observation.observation: The existing Monad USDm/USDC getAmountOut ladder is flat at -3.9 bps through its largest $100,000 quote, but this is not pooled with or substituted for Celo depth.

exit_capacity.capacity_basis: The USDC side of the mento_fpmm book at block timestamp 1789198433. A fixed-price maker quotes one rate at every size, so the ceiling on an exit is inventory, not slippage: you cannot receive more USDC than the book holds.
exit_capacity.cost_note: On a fixed-price venue ALL of the cost is in the level and NONE is in the curve. Marginal impact is 0 by construction, which is why no depth figure is published.

quoter_evidence.note: The venue quote function does NOT bound on inventory: it returns the same rate for sizes far exceeding the counter asset it would have to pay out. A quote is therefore not an executability statement here.
